task_instance: Instrument a small Node.js refund service (POST /api/orders/:id/refund) end-to-end per the skill's process: wrote the 2-4 on-call questions first (questions.md), added structured JSON logging with mandatory correlation IDs and an entry-point field distinguishing the HTTP endpoint from a simulated 'scheduler' reconciliation job reusing the same business logic (logger.js, server.js), added RED metrics (request rate/errors/duration histogram for the HTTP route, plus the external provider dependency) with bounded label sets and Prometheus-text exposition (metrics.js), wrote a symptom-based two-severity alert config referencing a runbook (alerts.yaml, docs/runbooks/refund-high-error-rate.md), and verified the telemetry itself by driving real HTTP traffic and a direct scheduler-entry-point call through success, validation-failure, and two induced-provider-failure paths, then confirming (a) every log line is valid structured JSON, (b) the induced failure is locatable purely by requestId without reading source, (c) both entry points appear correctly tagged, and (d) /metrics exposes counters/histograms with the expected 2xx/4xx/5xx labels and bucket data.
blocker_detail: Real production observability backends (prom-client, @opentelemetry/sdk-node, an actual Prometheus/Grafana/PagerDuty stack) are not installed and could not be installed offline, so tracing spans and true PromQL evaluation were not exercised. This did not block the core deliverable: the skill itself states the RED/USE rules and structured-logging discipline are vendor-neutral and identical regardless of backend, so hand-built structured logging + a metrics registry in Prometheus text format + an alert/runbook config demonstrate the same principles and were fully verified. Recorded here only as a scope note, not as the reason for the outcome.
tools_used: node (built-in http/crypto modules only, no npm packages)
